name: Return YouTube Subscribers
summary: See exact subscriber counts on YouTube again: on channel pages, under videos, and in search results.
tagline: Exact subscriber counts, back on YouTube.
safariPromotionalText: YouTube rounds every subscriber count. Return YouTube Subscribers puts the full number back on channel pages, watch pages and search results.
description: Since September 2019 YouTube has rounded every subscriber count: "1.2M subscribers" could mean anything from 1,200,000 to 1,299,999. Return YouTube Subscribers puts the full number back.
WHAT IT DOES
• Channel pages: "526M subscribers" becomes "526,594,749 subscribers"
• Watch pages: the exact count appears under the channel name on every video
• Search results: exact counts on channel results
• Real counts for creators in NextCounts' Unabbreviated Project, estimates for everyone else
• Keeps working as you browse; no page reloads needed
• Sort channel search results by exact subscriber count
• Exact counts on featured channels and channel lists
• Live streams: the count refreshes every 10 seconds, with rolling digits
• Full-screen live counter, and race mode to watch two channels side by side
• Save a shareable image of any count or race
• On your own channel: next milestone, subscribers to go and a projected date
• Toolbar popup ranking the channels you've viewed by how fast they're growing
• Choose exact (526,594,749) or compact (526.5M) numbers
• Hover any count to see where it came from and when it was updated
HOW IT WORKS

YouTube no longer publishes exact counts. The extension reads the ID of the channel you are viewing. If the channel is in NextCounts' Unabbreviated Project, you see its real count from YouTube Studio. Otherwise you see a live estimate from Mixerno.space, which can differ slightly from YouTube's internal figure. Hover a count to see which one it is.
PRIVACY
• No account, no sign-in, nothing to configure
• No analytics, ads or tracking inside the extension
• Growth history stays on your device
• The only data sent anywhere is the public ID of the channel you are viewing, to NextCounts or Mixerno.space, to look up its count
• Open source on GitHub

dataDisclosure.summary: The extension sends the public channel ID of the YouTube channel being viewed to api.nextcounts.com / api-v2.nextcounts.com (only for channels in NextCounts' Unabbreviated Project) or backend.mixerno.space to look up its subscriber count. Nothing else is collected, stored remotely or sold.
chromeDataTypes: Web history (the ID of the YouTube channel currently being viewed)
dataDisclosure.singlePurpose: Show exact, unabbreviated subscriber counts on YouTube in place of YouTube's rounded counts.
dataDisclosure.hostPermissionJustification: backend.mixerno.space returns the estimated subscriber count for a channel ID. NextCounts (api.nextcounts.com, api-v2.nextcounts.com) returns the real Studio count for channels that opted in, and is reached through its public CORS API without extra permissions. youtube.com access is needed to read the channel ID and replace the rounded count on the page.
dataDisclosure.reviewerNotes: To test: open any YouTube channel page (for example https://www.youtube.com/@YouTube) or video. The rounded count under the channel name (e.g. "14.2M subscribers") is replaced with the full number: from https://api-v2.nextcounts.com/api/youtube/channel/<channelId> for channels in NextCounts' Unabbreviated Project (list: https://api.nextcounts.com/api/youtube/studio/channels), otherwise from https://backend.mixerno.space/api/youtube/estv3/<channelId>. No minification or bundling is used; the submitted main.js is the source.
